data.description:
## Description

A worktree cleanup process (likely `harvest-worktree.sh` or a periodic GitHub Actions cleanup workflow) erroneously closed PR #231 (epic b575 session→main) shortly after creation, before any merge action was taken. The PR had passing initial CI checks (Hook Tests, Lint, ShellCheck, etc.), the llm-review job was in progress, and the user had not requested closure.

## Evidence

- PR #231 created at 2026-05-19T00:46:18Z (from gh log)
- PR #231 closed at 2026-05-19T00:49:59Z (~3.5 minutes later)
- No close action initiated by user or orchestrator in this session
- PR was not merged (state: CLOSED, not MERGED)
- User reported: "Our PR was erroneously closed by worktree cleanup"

## Impact

- Forces manual re-creation of the PR
- Loses any CI runs that were in progress (waste of compute + restart latency for llm-review which takes ~20 min)
- Disrupts the merge cascade for epic completion
- Could silently drop work if the user doesn't notice the closure

## Suspected mechanism

The cleanup process may be matching session/story branches with associated PRs and closing them as part of a "complete" or "merged" worktree cleanup. The matching logic likely doesn't distinguish between:
- A worktree that has been merged AND its PR successfully resolved
- A worktree that has an OPEN PR still in progress

## Suggested remediation

1. Audit the worktree cleanup process for code paths that close PRs
2. Add guard: do NOT close any PR that is in OPEN state with non-trivial CI runs in flight
3. Add guard: do NOT close any PR that the user has not explicitly requested closed
4. Surface logging when the cleanup considers closing a PR — silent closure is the worst outcome

## Related
- Companion architectural bugs: 576b-a6c7-3de3-4eef (per-sub-PR llm-review gap), 69e5-824a-ec7e-4bd9 (workflows gated to base=main)
- Surfaced during: epic b575 merge cascade (PR #231 closed mid-CI)
data.title: Worktree cleanup process erroneously closes open PRs (e.g., session->main epic PR)
